Alternaria_Leaf_Spot.quote: Leaf symptoms include round, brown spots with concentric rings.
Head rot symptoms can first appear as small brown spots on an otherwise healthy head.

Bacterial_Soft_Rot.quote: Early symptoms of bacterial soft rot include small water-soaked areas that later expand causing the tissue to become soft and mushy.
Damaged foliage showing soft, mushy, rotted head.

Black_Rot.quote: Leaf infections often result in a small, wilted, V-shaped infected area that extends inward from the leaf edge toward the midrib.
A typical cross-section of an infected stem or petiole shows a black ring due to invasion of the water-conducting vessels.
Dwarfing or one-sided growth is common both in individual leaves and in entire plants.

Downy_Mildew.quote: Small, angular lesions develop on leaves and inflorescences. These lesions enlarge and become irregular, yellow to orange necrotic patches
dark gray spots may appear on the curd and, when cut open, gray streaking is noticeable on the branches beneath the florets
